definition_en: not many, or a small number that does exist
core_image: 聚会桌上只剩三块饼干，来的人却很多
scene: 聚会桌上只剩三块饼干，来的人却很多。Few people came to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 few 是「很少的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是来参加聚会的人很少。

senses.title: Not many
senses.example: Few people came to the party.
senses.why: Few comes from Old English feawe, 'not many'; standing alone it keeps the negative force, so few people means almost none.
senses.whyCN: few 源自古英语 feawe「不多」；单独使用时保留否定意味，所以 few people 表示几乎没有。

senses.title: A small number
senses.example: I have a few friends here.
senses.why: With a before it, the same word turns positive: a few means a small number that is still there.
senses.whyCN: 前面加 a 时，同一个词转为肯定：a few 表示数量虽小但确实存在。

senses.title: The small group
senses.definition: the small group, as a pronoun
senses.definitionCN: 指人数不多的那一小群
senses.example: The few who came stayed till the end.
senses.exampleCN: 来的少数人一直留到最后。
senses.why: Used with the, few names a definite small group rather than a vague shortage.
senses.whyCN: 与 the 连用时，few 指某一确定的小群体，而不是笼统的短缺。

definition_en: a large area covered with trees, such land as a type, or a dense stand of upright things
core_image: 清晨的森林里，松树一直排到山坡尽头
scene: 清晨的森林里，松树一直排到山坡尽头。We walked through the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 forest 是「森林」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们穿过森林。

senses.title: A wooded area
senses.definition: a large area covered with trees
senses.example: We walked through the forest.
senses.why: Forest comes from Medieval Latin forestis silva, 'the outside wood'; it named woodland kept apart from the village fields.
senses.whyCN: forest 源自中世纪拉丁语 forestis silva「外围的林地」，指与村庄田地分开的树林。

senses.title: Woodland as a type
senses.definition: a large stretch of woodland, dense or open
senses.example: Much of the country is forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家大部分地区是林地。
senses.why: The same word can name the land type rather than one specific wood, as when a whole region is called forest.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也可以指土地类型而不是某一片树林，比如把整个地区称为林地。

senses.title: A dense stand
senses.definition: a large number of upright things
senses.example: A forest of poles stood around the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 舞台四周立着一片杆子。
senses.why: Because a forest is a crowd of tall trunks, English uses it for any dense stand of upright objects.
senses.whyCN: 因为森林是成片高耸的树干，英语就用它比喻任何密集竖立的东西。

definition_en: a tool with prongs, to divide into branches, or to lift with a fork
core_image: 餐盘旁边摆着一把银色餐叉，叉齿朝上
scene: 餐盘旁边摆着一把银色餐叉，叉齿朝上。He ate the cake with a fork.
sceneCN: 这里 fork 是「叉子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他用叉子吃蛋糕。

senses.title: A pronged tool
senses.definition: a tool with prongs for eating or lifting
senses.definitionCN: 带齿的进食或取物工具
senses.example: He ate the cake with a fork.
senses.why: Fork comes from Latin furca, a two-pronged pitchfork; the table tool kept the shape and the name.
senses.whyCN: fork 源自拉丁语 furca，即两齿的干草叉；餐具保留了它的形状和名字。

senses.title: To split in two
senses.example: The road forks after the bridge.
senses.why: The shape of a two-pronged fork gave the verb its sense: a path that splits looks like the two prongs.
senses.whyCN: 两齿叉的形状给出了动词义：分开的路就像叉子的两个齿。

senses.title: To lift with a fork
senses.definition: to lift or move with a fork
senses.example: She forked the meat onto the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 她用叉子把肉叉到盘子里。
senses.why: English made a verb from the noun, so to fork is to use the tool that bears its name.
senses.whyCN: 英语由名词造出动词，to fork 就是使用名为 fork 的工具。
